properties.description:
Author and owner of reflow2. Decides the design — the human in the three-party loop (dec:three-party-checks). **100% of reflow2's actual development is his** (stated 2026-08-18); other people named in this graph are USERS whose reports are field evidence, not developers.

═══ BACKGROUND — in his own words, 2026-08-18 ═══
**Develops software.** Career background is **space acquisitions and systems engineering** (Space Force). **BS Electrical Engineering; MS Electrical Engineering in electro-optics, focused on space object detection.** UAF/DoDAF-fluent.

⭐ THE TRAINING AND THE DAY JOB DIVERGE, AND THE DIVERGENCE IS THE USEFUL PART. He writes software, but he did not come up through software — he came through acquisition and hard EE. So requirements, cost, risk, verification and lifecycle are his FIRST instincts, and signal-versus-noise is a physical intuition rather than a metaphor. That is why an over-engineered answer reads to him as a failure mode with a name, and why "what did you actually measure?" is his standing question.

═══ PERSONA — how to speak to him ═══
First trial of `dec:idea-a-user-carries-a-persona-that-shapes-every-reply`. **Stored in `description` because Contributor has no persona field; whether it deserves one is the open question in that decision.** Agent-drafted from prior sessions, then corrected and enriched by him — which is the SELF-DESCRIBED vs ASSIGNED distinction that decision says is load-bearing.

⭐ **HIS LENS IS NOT "SIMPLIFY" — IT IS A VOCABULARY SWAP, AND GETTING THIS BACKWARDS WOULD PATRONISE HIM.** Requirement, interface, allocation, verification, TRL, KPP, blast radius, signal-to-noise are his native language and must NOT be softened. What he wants dropped is **reflow2's INTERNAL vocabulary** — gap, loop, detector, node id, "the loop owes" — and anything needing knowledge of how the tool is built to follow the sentence. Say what it MEANS for the design, then name the mechanism only if it earns its place.

· **Lead with a recommendation, always, unasked.** Options he can pick from, recommended one first and marked, every option carrying its consequence — including the ones not recommended. `req:a-question-arrives-with-a-reading`, accepted on his word; having to ask for it again is itself the defect.
· **Give him the honest counter-argument.** He overrules recommendations and that is useful; one with no stated counterweight reads as steering.
· **Numbers over impressions.** He notices when a claim was asserted rather than measured. Say plainly what was not checked.
· **Watch for over-engineering** — from the acquisitions side; *"engineers often over design something, it is kind of their nature."* A simple answer that fits is the better answer.
· **Fix at the root, never patch around** — standing, and he wants it built into reflow2 itself.
· **Second person to him; third person in this record**, because other people read the graph.

· **He thinks across domains, and it is part of how he creates** — in his words, 2026-09-27: *"I often like to look at things in one domain and then transfer that to another domain."* He reached the one-design rules through "blueprint" and "photocopy". Meeting him in an analogy he brings is working WITH him, not simplifying for him. And he ruled the same day: *"in the actual design graph, they should be in terms of what they actually are."* The analogy stays in the conversation; the record says what the thing is.

⚠️ FOR ANY OTHER READER: this describes how to TALK to him. It must never shape what gets written INTO the design — the record stays in its own register whoever is in the room.
